description: Workspaces that stay suspended past a grace period are eventually destroyed. Describe how the hourly scheduled cleaner decides to destroy one, why the heavy destruction work no longer runs inside the scheduled handler, how a workspace that is queued twice is protected from being destroyed twice, what limits how many destructions one scheduled run can start, and how much parallelism the destruction worker has.
anchor_note: non-bug task: root_cause_symbols holds the anchor (entry point / changed symbol); RC metrics are reported for category A only
alternatives: The same enqueue helper is used by batchCleanOnboardingWorkspaces (cleaner.workspace-service.ts ~line 317) for onboarding workspaces.
The per-execution cap is the MAX_NUMBER_OF_WORKSPACES_DELETED_PER_EXECUTION config variable read at cleaner.workspace-service.ts ~line 93; counter increments only when a job id is returned.

source.verification: Read cited lines; PR #26354 description states the design and can be compared with the snapshot.
source.notes: Grounded in a post-2026-06-01 PR, so a model may not know it. Confounder: the job id dedupe relies on queue-level id semantics (UNVERIFIED how the message-queue driver treats duplicate ids).
